stories.question: What happens when someone sends a message?
stories.answer: Ada's client sends it to the host, which accepts it, tells every client it is busy and asks the model. When the model is done the host settles the turn and tells everyone it is idle again.

steps.text: Ada types a question and presses send in her panel
Her client chart sends it to the host as input.submit
The host accepts it, logs it, tells every client it is busy, and starts a turn
Every client marks the host as busy
The host invokes the model with the conversation
The model starts writing
The model finishes; the host settles the turn
The host tells every client it is idle
The clients are ready for the next message

stories.question: How does the model get tools run on other people's machines?
stories.answer: The model asks for tools; the host sends each call to the client that provides that tool, all at once, and waits. Each client runs the tool locally and sends the result back; when all are in, the host asks the model again.

steps.text: The model starts a tool call (shell)
…and a second one (python) in the same answer
The host sends shell to the terminal and python to the Python client, at once, and waits
The terminal runs the shell command
The Python client runs the python code at the same time
The shell result comes back first
The python result comes back
With every result in, the host asks the model again

stories.question: What if I send while the model is busy?
stories.answer: Your message waits in your own client's queue. When the host says it is idle, your client sends it and it gets its own turn.

steps.text: Bo types while the model is writing
His client knows the host is busy, so the message waits in his queue
The turn ends (here: Ada stops it) and the host tells everyone it is idle
Bo's client sees the host idle and sends the queued message
The host accepts it and starts Bo's own turn
The model is asked about Bo's message

stories.question: How do I change its course mid-answer?
stories.answer: Steer: a steer waits in the host's inbox and rides along with the tool results into the next request. Only people with the control role may steer; Bo's attempt is refused and goes back into his editor.

steps.text: Bo tries to steer
The host refuses: Bo lacks the control role
Bo's client puts the text back into his editor
Ada steers while the tools run
The host accepts and holds the steer in its inbox
The tool result arrives
Tool results and Ada's steer go to the model together

stories.question: How does stop work?
stories.answer: A person with the control role interrupts; the host cancels the model request, discards the half-written answer and is idle at once, so the next queued message can go.

steps.text: The scenario has Ada press stop
Ada's client sends input.interrupt
The host leaves the turn, cancelling the model request
The half-written answer is discarded from the log
Everyone hears the host is idle
Bo's queued message can go now

stories.question: What happens when a client drops offline and returns?
stories.answer: The client notices and stops expecting messages; when it is back it asks the host to resync, gets a fresh snapshot and is live again.

steps.text: Bo's network drops
Bo's client goes offline
The network comes back
Bo's client asks the host to resync
The host sends a snapshot and its current state
Bo's client is live again

stories.question: How does a newcomer catch up?
stories.answer: A new client says hello; the host welcomes it, adds it to the roster and sends a snapshot of the history, after which the client is live.

steps.text: The Python client starts and says hello
The host welcomes it and adds it to the roster
The client becomes a member and starts syncing
The host sends a snapshot of the conversation
With the snapshot applied, the client is live

worlds.change: The model is overloaded: every request for Ada's two-tool question fails with a 529
worlds.outcome: The host backs off and retries four times (1, 2, 4, 8 s), each attempt overloaded too; after the fifth it gives up, logs the error and tells everyone it is idle. No tools run.

worlds.change: The Python client's network drops while its python call is pending
worlds.outcome: The shell result comes back, the python one never does; after the host's 30 s tool timeout it sends the model what it has and the turn ends.

worlds.change: Ada presses stop while the model is still writing her answer
worlds.outcome: The host discards the half-written answer and is idle at once; the model never asks for tools, so no client runs anything.

worlds.change: The Python client never joins, so nobody provides the python tool
worlds.outcome: The model still asks for both tools; only the shell goes out, the python call has no provider, and the model answers with what it got.
